question: What is the natural animal reservoir host for the Ebola virus?
explanation: Fruit bats belonging to the Pteropodidae family serve as the primary natural reservoir host for the Ebola virus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h1)

question: The Filoviridae family includes which specific disease-causing agent?
explanation: Ebola virus is classified under the Filoviridae family, known for causing severe hemorrhagic fevers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h1)

question: Primary transmission of the Ebola virus requires contact with what substance?
explanation: Ebola transmits primarily through direct contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h2)

question: A community member preparing a deceased relative for burial is at highest risk of what?
explanation: Corpses remain highly infectious after death, making traditional handling a major transmission risk during outbreaks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which symptom characterizes the early dry stage of Ebola Virus Disease?

options.A: Sudden high fever and severe headache

explanation: The initial days of EVD feature abrupt flu-like symptoms including high fever, severe headache, and profound weakness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why does early clinical diagnosis of Ebola remain difficult in local clinics?

options.A: Skin rashes never appear during the first week
options.B: Early signs mimic common endemic infections like malaria
options.D: Patients refuse to report fever during the daytime

explanation: Initial symptoms like fever, fatigue, and muscle aches closely resemble malaria, typhoid, and other common tropical diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the standard laboratory test used to confirm an Ebola infection?

options.A: Ziehl-Neelsen sputum microscopy for acid-fast bacilli
options.D: Rapid diagnostic test strip for typhoid antibodies

explanation: RT-PCR is the gold standard laboratory test for detecting viral RNA in blood and other fluid samples. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h4)

question: How many days is the maximum incubation period nurses look for in contact histories?
explanation: The incubation period for Ebola ranges from 2 to 21 days, establishing the standard window for monitoring contacts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h4)

question: What forms the core of medical management for patients with Ebola?

options.A: Aggressive supportive care and fluid replacement
options.B: Complete restriction of all fluid intake
options.C: Immediate surgical removal of the spleen

explanation: Supportive care focusing on fluid, electrolyte balance, and treating symptoms significantly improves patient survival rates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is prompt correction of fluid loss vital in Ebola management?

options.A: To prevent hypovolemic shock from severe diarrhea and vomiting
options.B: To speed up the clearance of viral load from red blood cells
options.C: To lower the body temperature without using any medications
options.D: To stop the patient from developing a secondary skin rash

explanation: Profuse vomiting and watery diarrhea cause rapid intravascular volume depletion, leading quickly to fatal shock if untreated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h5)

question: What chlorine concentration is recommended for disinfecting contaminated surfaces during an outbreak?
explanation: A 0.5% chlorine solution is standard for environmental decontamination and cleaning surfaces exposed to viral fluids. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why must suspected Ebola patients be placed in immediate isolation upon arrival?

options.A: To prevent family members from bringing forbidden local foods
options.B: To comply with administrative rules without clinical benefit
options.C: To ensure they receive specialized high-cost surgical procedures
options.D: To prevent nosocomial transmission to other patients and staff

explanation: Immediate isolation halts the spread of the virus within the healthcare facility, protecting vulnerable patients and workers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h6)

question: How long must identified contacts of an Ebola patient be actively monitored?
explanation: Monitoring contacts for 21 days covers the full incubation span to catch any new onset of symptoms early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of community contact tracing during an outbreak?

options.A: To distribute free antimalarial drugs to every household
options.B: To punish individuals who fail to report their travel history
options.C: To gather statistics for international research publications
options.D: To find new infections early and isolate them quickly

explanation: Contact tracing ensures that secondary cases are identified and isolated before they can spread the virus further. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h7)

question: Which complication is commonly reported by survivors of Ebola Virus Disease?

options.A: Total loss of long-term memory function
options.B: Joint and muscle pain (arthralgia and myalgia)

explanation: Persistent joint and muscle pain are hallmark features of Post-Ebola Syndrome experienced by many survivors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h8)

question: Why can recovered male patients transmit the virus weeks after clinical recovery?

options.A: Bone marrow continues to manufacture infected white blood cells
options.B: Antibodies produced during infection turn into active viral particles
options.C: The virus persists in immunologically privileged sites like semen
options.D: The virus reactivates when exposed to bright sunlight

explanation: Ebola can linger in certain body compartments such as the testes, allowing sexual transmission long after recovery. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h8)
